text:
git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): every exception an SPL class raised claimed to come from line 0

php reports the CALL SITE for an exception an internal method throws, because
the `new` behind it lives in php-src and has no php line of its own. elephc's
builtin SPL classes are compiled from SYNTHESIZED bodies, whose `new` carries no
span either — so the payload's creation line was zero and stayed zero.

Zero is not a line php ever prints, and it showed in three places at once:
`getLine()` answered `0`, `getFile()` was right but useless without it, and the
uncaught report dropped BOTH its ` in FILE:LINE` suffix and its `  thrown in …
on line N` tail, because the writer skips the location when the line is zero.

MEASURED against `(new SplFileInfo("nope"))->getSize()`, which php reports at
the line of the `getSize()` call, and `new DirectoryIterator("nope")`, which it
reports at the `new`.

The line is published into `_rt_internal_call_line` at each call INTO a class
whose bodies are synthetic, and the throwable allocator reads it exactly when it
has no span of its own. An ordinary method call on a user class publishes
nothing, so it pays nothing; a user `new` keeps its own span, which is why
`new RuntimeException(…)` still reports the line it is written on.

`$obj->$name()` on a builtin class made the same widening necessary in the scanf
gate: the dynamic ladder emits every method of the classes a program constructs,
`SplFileObject::fscanf()` among them, whose body calls an engine that was not
being injected — a LINK failure, not a diagnostic.
